reconcile.note: Keil and Delitzsch read Joshua's total-victory language as gradual dispossession, not immediate conquest, so Joshua 21's fulfillment survives despite unconquered enclaves.

discrepancy.note: Paine notes Judges and 2 Samuel's silence about wiping out the Jebusites undercuts Joshua's claims of total conquest, since the Jebusites plainly survived in Jerusalem.

quotes.text: It is not said, either in Samuel or in Chronicles, that they "utterly destroyed men, women and children, that they left not a soul to breathe," as is said of their other conquests; and the silence here observed implies that it was taken by capitulation; and that the Jebusites, the native inhabitants, continued to live in the place after it was taken.
quotes.attr: Thomas Paine (d. 1809), The Age of Reason, Part II (1795), ch. I, on Joshua 15:63, Judges 1:21, and 2 Samuel 5:4-9.

sides.snippet: Yahweh gave them rest round about, according to all that he swore to their fathers: and there stood not a man of all their enemies before them; Yahweh delivered all their enemies into their hand.
sides.verseText: Yahweh gave them rest round about, according to all that he swore to their fathers: and there stood not a man of all their enemies before them; Yahweh delivered all their enemies into their hand.

sides.snippet: The children of Benjamin did not drive out the Jebusites who inhabited Jerusalem; but the Jebusites dwell with the children of Benjamin in Jerusalem to this day.
sides.verseText: The children of Benjamin did not drive out the Jebusites who inhabited Jerusalem; but the Jebusites dwell with the children of Benjamin in Jerusalem to this day.
